So what is Slime Rancher? You are Beatrix Lebeaux a girl who recently bought the ranch on the far far range to start a new life for herself. Your ultimate goal in the game is to sell plorts. Which is like slime poop. You build up your ranch with corrals, gardens, silos, etc, Buy upgrades and find more and and better ways to collect and harvest plorts.

Would I Recommend this game to anyone?

Yes I would recommend this game to everyone. The game has amazing style of art, Has super cute slimes, And a great deal of exploration, The game also has a fair decent amount of Achievements for those who like achievement hunting! They also add new content fairly regularly.

I hope this review helped you for deciding to buy this game or not. P.s Really suggest you buy it! You won't regret it! ;)

This game is really awesome, reminds me of Minecraft (when it was considered to be a good game). Here the pros and cons.

Pros:
+ Originality. Have you played farms/rancho simulators? But of course! Have you played pseudo-survival games? Yes, we did. Have you played a game about slimes? Well, yeah... So, where is the originality you will ask. Then answer me: have you all of the above in one game with fps-like interface? And I will answer: no, you did not.

+ Graphics. This is about the colorfullness of the game. It is really important in such games.

+ Everything is cute, nothing more to add.

+ Interesting system. At first you have to get slimes, then you learn how to feed them, and then those bastards are jumping out of their cages to get some food from the nearest garden. And the things are only getting started. Lots of features are everywhere.

Cons:

- WTF is going on? It was my question for the first 10 minutes of play. The game is really confusing at the start.

- Limitted world. Yeah, it is not very big, and you will soon find yourself doing nothing. It is about 6-7 hours of play, so it is hardly a disadvantage.

So it covers everything I had to say. Game is really cool, though the price is a bit high (waited for a discount).
8.75/10

Slime Rancher is a fun and stylized escape from reality that works differently from other farm/ranch based games. Rather than purchase your livestock and crops, you're left to adventure and pick up what you can before returning your haul back to the ranch. From there you will maintain your bubbly little creatures in corals, usually divided by species to avoid an outbreak of Tarr, corrupt slimes that will eat your entire population. You feed the creatures and collect their "product" to sell on a galactic market. All the while you'll be doing missions for cash and/or new slime fodder.

I was perhaps at my closest to finding inner peace while playing this game. Nothing to worry about really, with enough challenge and progression to keep a person hooked. The discovery of new biomes and new slimes was exciting every time.

I have obtained every achievement outside of Rush Mode for now, but I'm sure I'll get to that sometime.

I liked the first half of the game where you are organising your ranch, opening up the tech tree, combining slimes, working the market system, shooting plorts. The variety of slimes is so fun, and trying to figure out what you've done wrong and trying to fix it led to funny shenanigans. The game has the juice, from the movement, actions, music, and especially the sound effects.

The second half, tho, abandons the progression of the slime/plort types in favour of map unlocking, a magic water system, and an underwhelming ending. I failed to connect with the special maps that each trading NPC opened up for you because I didn't see an endgame beyond the H story points. It was like the game turned into a Talos Principle-like for a few hours but without the metaphysical catharsis. I wanted more Factorio-style optimization mechanics, such as the ability to conduct my drones more efficiently (why are so many of my corrals going hungry while one is FULL on beets?). By the time I would be able to make use of the fully upgraded mechanics, I had lost steam on what I was doing. So many slime types that I didn't really end up needing in the end.

So, fun game for a couple dozen hours!! Definitely buy and play! By when you unlock the last map don't be surprised if you wind up as confused as to what was going on as I was.

what i like most about slime rancher is that it's a game that all people can get into. the world is immediately immersive, with a relaxing soundtrack, cute art and loveable characters. the world is incredibly large and intimidating at first, but when you're in the endgame it all feels very manageable, though it of course takes quite a while before you have a good grasp on the environment and don't need to check the map consistently, because there really is a LOT of terrain.

if you like casual, simulation or open world games this is definitely top tier.

the main character is a woman of colour with an ambiguously gendered love interest which is nice to see, and you learn more about them and their life through letters. while the character storylines aren't the most interesting part of the game, it's a nice little anchor that might make you feel some nostaliga and longing for a life you never even lived.

tldr.text: Overwhelmingly Positive (98%): players praise the story and characters, and the graphics and art.
The most common complaints cover the price, the content and grind, and bugs and crashes.

details.text: Recent reviews complain less often about the grind and about bugs and crashes than all-time reviews do, and they stay about as positive as the all-time score.
Players with under 2 hours are far less positive, at 85%, than players with 10 to 50 hours, at 99%, and one early complaint is "The grind early on is terrible".
